name: Placement gate
question: Accept the four open gate items and put this placement on the board in a PR?
why_now: Every block is approved (D04–D08) and the rest of the board is placed. The gate passes 11 of 15 checks. The four it fails were all known before this run, or come from how the router works, not from where the parts sit. Each needs your call before the placement goes onto `node60.kicad_pcb`.

facts.label: Passes
facts.value: floorplan intent (0 errors); heights on the bottom (6.17 mm), under the low lid (9.0 mm) and under the lid bosses (5.03 mm); U401 BGA escape (4 signal layers, 4 available); layer capacity (no window over 60 %); both buck hot loops; every approved block on its table pose (power, T1S, both bucks, crystal, three output cells); fiducials 3 per side; net classes; via room at all 9 high-current pads

facts.label: Moved against main
facts.value: 52 parts: the power-entry block, the crystal's C424, C425 and TP407, the U601 and U801 cells, TP402 (0.2 mm off TP407)

facts.label: One change after approval
facts.value: C803 (U801's VDD decap) moved 0.05 mm further from J908 after D08, so its courtyard clears J908's by KRT's measure; recorded in U801's table

facts.label: Search speed
facts.value: pose_search.py placed TP806 and cleared five courtyard touches in about 5 s each run (the old per-pose loop took about 30 min for one part)

facts.label: Busbar overlaps
facts.value: Each busbar footprint (BB901, BB902) carries a tie pad inside each REDCUBE terminal's pad, so the board shows the bar joining its two terminals (D02, option A). Two parts' pads in one place is never legal to KRT, and it can't waive locked parts, so check_assembly says NOT BUILDABLE. KiCad's own DRC accepts them (net tie). Accepting means REPORT.md names these four as by design.

facts.label: Schematic parity
facts.value: kicad-cli reports the same counts on main's `node60.kicad_pcb`, so they predate this run. C207 and L201 have no footprint on the board; the 56 mismatches are footprints that differ from their symbol's; the 199 are field values. Follow-up: a schematic/library pass before routing sign-off.
facts.source: kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity on both boards

facts.label: U501 pin 29 and the PHY's south edge
facts.value: Pins 26–31 sit at 0.5 mm pitch: RBIAS, REFCLK, an unused pin, 3V3_MAIN, then the T1S pair. Every pin reads PASSABLE (a route exists). Each order tried closes some and loses others: REFCLK and RBIAS first left only pin 29 open; 3V3_MAIN first left 3 open, the T1S pair among them; REFCLK and RBIAS after the T1S pair (the chain's order now, since T1S has priority) left REFCLK and CRS_DV. The cause found: the bulk pass rips all of 3V3_MAIN, pin 29's fan-out stub included, to make room, and restores 67 of its 68 connections. 3V3_MAIN has endpoints in the moved output cells, so this board changes its routing order; the PHY's parts did not move. Follow-up for real routing: hand-route the PHY's south edge first (pin 29 straight out to a via, then REFCLK and RBIAS).

options.name: Accept the four items, open the PR
options.summary: Put the composed placement on `node60.kicad_pcb` (busbars, fiducials and rule areas kept), write REPORT.md, and open a PR for your review. Each item below goes into REPORT.md as accepted, with its follow-up.

measures.value: 2 blocking: U501 pin 29, and VBAT_IN's J901–J910 join, which only the busbar makes

gains: The approved blocks on the board now; routing can start
Each open item has a stated reason and owner
costs: The skill's DONE rule (0 open by KRT and by the board's rules) is not met; REPORT.md says so

options.name: Fix the schematic parity first
options.summary: Before the PR, bring the schematic and the board into line: add C207 and L201's footprints, and resolve the 56 footprint/symbol and 199 field mismatches.
costs: Schematic and library work, not placement: none of it comes from this run, so it holds up the placement without changing it

options.name: Keep working the PHY route
options.summary: Keep changing the fast route's order until one run closes every net at the PHY.
gains: The DONE rule met in this run
costs: It has not converged: each order closes one PHY net and loses another

recommendation.why: None of the four comes from where the parts sit, and each has a follow-up that does not need the placement to change.

answer: Reply with A, B or C, or a change.
